# The labloop cookbook

Worked examples: a real task, the real commands, and the run's real output —
including the trials that were thrown away, which are most of the information.

**This file is generated by `build_index.py`. Do not edit it by hand.**

Start with [Let Claude Code optimize real code](02-proposers/agent-optimizes-real-code/)
if you want to see what a loop actually looks like, and
[Four experiments, four noise levels](noise-across-recipes.md) for what they say
together. See [PROPOSAL.md](PROPOSAL.md) for what this is and
[CANDIDATES.md](CANDIDATES.md) for what is not built yet.

## Tiers

Every recipe declares how far it is verified, because the most useful ones
need a real agent or real hardware and cannot run in CI:

| Tier | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `verified` | runs end to end in CI |
| `structural` | runs in CI with the agent stubbed; wiring checked, not judgement |
| `narrative` | a real recorded run; not executed in CI |

### [Tune a classifier and watch the loop throw most of it away](01-first-loop/tune-a-classifier/)

## 02-proposers

### [Let Claude Code optimize real code against a real benchmark](02-proposers/agent-optimizes-real-code/)

*How do I point an actual coding agent at my code and only keep the speedups that are real?*

`narrative` · needs `claude-cli`, `network`
- the ten lines that turn $LABLOOP_BRIEF into an agent prompt
- measuring wall-clock noise before believing a speedup
- --min-delta and --confirm chosen from a real noise measurement
- protecting a correctness check, not just an eval script


## 03-real-tasks

### [Improve retrieval quality on a real corpus](03-real-tasks/improve-rag-retrieval/)

*How do I tune a retriever against a real query set without tuning it to the answers?*

`narrative` · needs `claude-cli`, `network`
- nDCG over recall@k, because a coarse metric ties and a tie reverts
- protecting queries and judgments, not the retriever
- a corpus built by importing so C modules are not silently missing
- a metric that goes up is not evidence your explanation is right

### [Optimize a prompt against a held-out eval set](03-real-tasks/optimize-a-prompt/)

*How do I let an agent rewrite a prompt without it learning the answer key?*

`narrative` · needs `claude-cli`, `network`
- a harness bug and a bad prompt produce the same low number
- spread: none can be a symptom of a broken harness, not a stable metric
- the eval harness should self-test before it scores anything
- mean field accuracy over whole-case accuracy, to avoid ties
- an exact tie reverts, seen on real data

### [Speed up a test suite without shrinking it](03-real-tasks/speed-up-a-test-suite/)

*How do I let an agent make my tests faster without letting it delete the slow ones?*

`narrative` · needs `claude-cli`, `network`, `pytest`
- protecting a property of the run (test count) instead of hashing files
- an acceptance check the agent cannot edit, behind editable unit tests
- wall-clock is not inherently noisy: this suite measured 0.1% spread
